title: What Makes a Chordate? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A fish in the pond, a tadpole in a puddle and you, a few weeks before you were born: very different animals, yet early in life all three had a stiff rod along the back, a tube of nerves above it and slits in the throat. Diya sees a fish embryo and a human embryo side by side in her textbook and asks why they look like cousins. The answer: both are chordates.

You will see a living, labelled diagram of the chordate body plan: the notochord, the dorsal hollow nerve cord and the paired pharyngeal gill slits, plus the post-anal tail and the closed circulation, then a cross-section that shows what dorsal, hollow and ventral really mean. An animated timeline follows the notochord through life in the three subphyla: Urochordata (Ascidia, only in the larval tail), Cephalochordata (Branchiostoma, head to tail for life) and Vertebrata (embryo only, then a vertebral column). Then the extra features of vertebrates, a fish vs cockroach comparison from NCERT Table 4.1, a pause and think check, a worked example that sorts four sea animals (including Balanoglossus), the exam trap about backbones, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 36 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
